transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Marcos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Lena (Aureon Procurement), Samir (Legal), Ruth (Cloud Security), Diego (Platform)
---
Summary: quick procurement/technical sync to align on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS/privileged keying, SLA routing tiers and a short pilot benchmark plan. Action items captured, next steps agreed.
---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick agenda — redline status, KMS/privileged keying path, SLA routing (gold/silver/fallback), and then the perf/pilot plan.
[00:18] Lena: thanks, yes we want to get the legal checklist out of the way, procurement timeline — we need approvals by end of next week ideally.
[00:27] Samir: hi, from legal i have three sticking points so far: DPA egress clauses, subprocessor list frequency, and indemnity cap language in section 7.
[00:41] Marcos: on the infra side we want to understand the private VPC option and how you handle customer-managed KMS/HSM; also service account RBAC and audit logs retention.
[00:55] Ruth: to add, SOC2 type II is a must, and we need to see audit log retention of at least 1 year, plus access to audit trails for privileged ops.
[01:08] Priya: noted — we have a standard RBAC template and an onboarding playbook, i'll drop links after the call.
[01:20] Diego: just to call out our constraint — we run in eu-west-1 and have strict data residency. any cross-region fallback must keep PII in-region or be anonymized.
[01:33] Avery: great, that's helpful. on the MSA/DPA side i'm expecting a couple of redline rounds; we can share a version with markup by friday. Samir, can you share the exact indemnity language you'd prefer?
[01:48] Samir: yes i'll send a clause suggestion, but we also need clarity on data subprocessor notification windows — 30 days is our baseline.
[02:02] Marcos: about KMS — Redwood supports two options: customer-managed KMS with CMK in their cloud account (we Integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS) or Redwood-managed with per-tenant envelope keys. For Aureon we recommend customer-managed for compliance.
[02:19] Ruth: ok customer-managed is preferred. do you support HSM-backed keys or BYOK?
[02:24] Marcos: yes HSM-backed keys via KMS, BYOK supported. small note: in the private deployment we can wire the key policy so Redwood never sees plaintext keys; there's some config on sidecar connectors.
[02:40] Lena: what about escrow for keys if we terminate? we need a defined handoff.
[02:46] Avery: we can define a key escrow/rotation procedure in the onboarding runbook. Priya will own the operational steps.
[02:55] Priya: i'll add the key rotation and escrow step to the onboarding checklist and include handoff runbooks.
[03:07] Diego: on networking — we need a diagram for egress and NAT, and clarity on port openings for dedicated bursts. can you share network diagram?
[03:15] Marcos: yes we'll share a VPC peering and private link diagram; note that we offer VPC endpoints for private plane control plane traffic.
[03:26] Samir: regarding DPA, one ask — data deletion certification after contract end, we need a signed confirmation of data purge with logs.
[03:36] Avery: we can provide deletion confirmations and a retention export; we also support configurable retention windows.
[03:44] Ruth: retention windows — can they be per-customer? some teams need 90 days only, others 365.
[03:51] Marcos: yes retention is configurable per route and per-model. technically we have prefix cache/KV cache controls (sometimes the transcriptor misses that term, we saw 'kayvee' cache) — we can purge prefixes per tenant.
[04:05] Lena: great. pricing questions — we ran a quick TCO and need to validate burst pricing and egress fees. procurement is worried about unexpected egress levy.
[04:16] Avery: we usually separate compute (per-token) and egress network fees. for Dedicated we provide committed throughput discounts; egress is billed at cost plus small margin — we can include a cap for the pilot.
[04:30] Lena: cap for pilot sounds good. financing prefers 30-day PO terms, is that possible?
[04:36] Avery: yes standard is net-30 PO for enterprise. we'll get legal billing contact details in the followup.
[04:45] Samir: also curious about SLA credits calculation — you mention p99 latency SLOs in the doc, how are credits calculated?
[04:55] Marcos: SLA credits are pro-rated by minute of unavailability vs monthly uptime targets; for latency SLOs we provide best-effort and have rollback policies to smaller models to preserve availability. we'll send the exact formula.
[05:12] Ruth: fallback is important. we need assurances that fallback keeps data in-region and that the fallback model is also quantized/compatible.
[05:22] Marcos: yes fallback policies are region-aware. for quantized models we maintain artifacts per-region. sometimes the model variant nomenclature gets munged in transcripts (you might see 'redwood-lite' or similar), but we maintain compatibility.
[05:37] Diego: for the pilot can we run a 48 hour ramp with synthetic traffic that mimics svc-prod? we want to test p95/p99 and mem footprint.
[05:46] Marcos: absolutely — recommend a 48-72 hour run on Dedicated pre-prod pool in eu-west-1 with KV cache warmups. i'll need sample traffic pattern (tokens/sec, seq length distribution).
[06:00] Diego: i'll produce the CSV sample traffic; can we also test cold-starts?
[06:04] Marcos: yes we can script cold-start cycles.
[06:10] Priya: i'll coordinate the pilot runbook and include post-mortem template.
[06:16] Lena: legal redlines — Samir will send the list. procurement needs final pricing approval before PO.
[06:24] Samir: one more legal ask — do you accept counterparty audit requests? we may want an SOC attestation for a narrow scope.
[06:33] Avery: we have SOC2 reports we can share under NDA. we also offer limited on-site or remote security questionnaires for enterprise customers.
[06:42] Ruth: good, we'll request the SOC report. also please include details on log retention and SIEM integration (splunk/kinesis).
[06:52] Marcos: we have an API for logs, can push to kinesis/Splunk, or ship syslogs; retention configurable.
[07:00] Lena: timeline check — procurement expects a redline review and pricing sheet by next thursday; can you commit to that?
[07:07] Avery: yes we'll aim for 2026-07-09 for the MSA/DPA redlines and pricing summary. Marcos will produce benchmark slots for 2026-07-11 to 07-13.
[07:19] Diego: any constraints about network egress IP ranges? we need static egress IPs for firewall allow-listing.
[07:25] Marcos: Dedicated provides static egress NAT IPs; hosted endpoints have a pool but can be whitelisted via PrivateLink. we'll include the list in the network artifact.
[07:36] Samir: curious about key rotation at termination: if keys are customer-managed and you request handoff, what's the exact step?
[07:44] Priya: operationally we run a key export handshake, we confirm rotation and then provide signed deletion certificates for Redwood copies. full steps in playbook.
[07:55] Avery: i'll attach playbook link in followup.
[08:02] Ruth: do you support in-place on-prem deployments (air-gapped)? we might need that for a regulated subset later.
[08:09] Marcos: yes we have a Private on-prem package; that is a different commercial path with lift-and-shift effort and a separate SLA. we can scope later if needed.
[08:22] Lena: for now pilot in VPC is fine. procurement question — any minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[08:29] Avery: Dedicated typically has a monthly reserve but we can do a limited pilot without long-term commit; pricing for pilot vs committed differs.
[08:38] Diego: last technical: what metrics will you expose during pilot? cpu/gpu utilization, token/sec, cache hit rate, p95/p99 lat.
[08:46] Marcos: yes all those plus per-route cost breakdown and tracing hooks.
[08:52] Samir: ok, next steps recap?
[08:56] Avery: recap — Avery to share redlines + pricing by 7/9; Marcos to run benchmark slot and share results by 7/12; Priya to send onboarding checklist and RBAC template; Samir to send DPA exceptions; Lena to confirm PO flow.
[09:12] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:16] Meeting end.
